account.name: Marlow Freight Systems
account.industry: transportation, logistics, supply chain and storage

dossier.summary: Marlow Freight Systems is a regional LTL carrier with 11 terminals across the Southeast and about 380 employees. It leases most of its fleet and buys fuel, tires and maintenance from around 300 vendors.
dossier.why_now: Announced a twelfth terminal in Savannah in September.

integrations.summary: A vendor approved in Plinth becomes a NetSuite vendor record, and a signed contract raises its purchase order. Bills and payment status come back, so the contract shows what has been paid.
integrations.syncs: Vendors, purchase orders, bills and payment status, every 15 minutes
integrations.setup: About an hour with a NetSuite admin, through a SuiteTalk integration role

integrations.summary: Vendors and bills sync between Plinth and QuickBooks, so a contract shows what has been billed against it without anyone retyping amounts.
integrations.syncs: Vendors, bills and payment status, hourly
integrations.setup: About 20 minutes; a QuickBooks admin signs in once

integrations.summary: Approved vendors and purchase orders flow from Plinth into Intacct, and posted bills flow back to the contract they belong to.
integrations.syncs: Vendors, purchase orders, bills and dimensions, every 30 minutes
integrations.setup: About an hour with an Intacct admin and a Web Services user

integrations.summary: Vendors and purchase orders approved in Plinth are created in Xero. Xero stays the book of record.
integrations.syncs: Vendors and purchase orders, Plinth to Xero, hourly
integrations.setup: About 15 minutes; a Xero admin signs in once

integrations.summary: Plinth reads cost centers, departments and manager relationships from Workday, so approval chains follow your org chart and every contract lands on the right cost center.
integrations.syncs: Workers, cost centers and supervisory orgs, Workday to Plinth, nightly
integrations.setup: Half a day with a Workday admin, through an integration system user

integrations.summary: Customer contracts start from a closed-won opportunity. Plinth pulls the account, the opportunity owner and the order form, so sales never emails a contract to legal.
integrations.syncs: Accounts, closed-won opportunities and attached files, Salesforce to Plinth, every 5 minutes
integrations.setup: About 30 minutes with a Salesforce admin; a connected app and one permission set

integrations.summary: A deal moved to closed won opens a customer contract in Plinth with the company, the deal owner and the quote attached.
integrations.syncs: Companies, closed-won deals and quotes, HubSpot to Plinth, every 5 minutes
integrations.setup: About 15 minutes; a HubSpot super admin signs in once

integrations.summary: Approvals, renewal reminders and questions on a contract land in Slack. An approver reads the summary and approves or sends it back from the message.
integrations.syncs: Approval requests, renewal reminders and comments, both ways, as they happen
integrations.setup: About 10 minutes; a workspace admin installs the Plinth app

integrations.summary: Approvals and renewal reminders arrive as Teams messages with the contract summary, and approvers act on them without opening Plinth.
integrations.syncs: Approval requests and renewal reminders, both ways, as they happen
integrations.setup: About 20 minutes; a Teams admin approves the Plinth app

integrations.summary: A contract leaves Plinth for signature in DocuSign and comes back signed, filed against the vendor, with the signed PDF and the audit trail.
integrations.syncs: Envelopes, signer status and signed PDFs, both ways, as they happen
integrations.setup: About 15 minutes with a DocuSign admin

integrations.summary: Contracts go out for signature from Plinth through Acrobat Sign and return signed, with the audit report attached.
integrations.syncs: Agreements, signer status and signed PDFs, both ways, as they happen
integrations.setup: About 15 minutes with an Acrobat Sign account admin

integrations.summary: People sign in to Plinth with Okta. SCIM creates and removes accounts as people join and leave, and Okta groups map to Plinth roles.
integrations.syncs: Users and groups, Okta to Plinth, as they change
integrations.setup: About 30 minutes with an Okta admin, SAML and SCIM

integrations.summary: Single sign-on through Entra ID, with SCIM provisioning so leavers lose access the day they leave.
integrations.syncs: Users and groups, Entra ID to Plinth, as they change
integrations.setup: About 30 minutes with an Entra admin, SAML and SCIM

integrations.summary: Sign in with Google, and Plinth files each signed contract's PDF in the Drive folder you choose.
integrations.syncs: Sign-in, plus signed PDFs to Drive, as they happen
integrations.setup: About 10 minutes; a Workspace admin approves the app

integrations.summary: A new vendor review or a security questionnaire opens a Jira issue in the queue you choose, and the contract links to it.
integrations.syncs: Issues, Plinth to Jira, as they are raised
integrations.setup: About 15 minutes with a Jira admin

integrations.summary: Every contract, vendor, spend commitment and renewal date lands in your Snowflake account as tables, refreshed nightly, for your own reporting.
integrations.syncs: Contracts, vendors, commitments and renewals, Plinth to Snowflake, nightly
integrations.setup: About an hour with a Snowflake admin, through a share

integrations.summary: If you are moving off Coupa, Plinth imports your supplier list and open contracts from a Coupa export, with the original IDs kept.
integrations.syncs: Suppliers and contracts, one-time import
integrations.setup: A working session with our team, usually one afternoon

integrations.summary: Plinth imports your Ironclad repository with its metadata, so no contract and no renewal date gets lost in a move.
integrations.syncs: Contracts, metadata and signed PDFs, one-time import
integrations.setup: A working session with our team, usually one afternoon

integrations.summary: Vendor card spend in Ramp shows up against the vendor's contract in Plinth, so you see what is contracted next to what is being spent.
integrations.syncs: Vendors and transactions, Ramp to Plinth, daily; vendor records, Plinth to Ramp
integrations.setup: About 10 minutes; a Ramp admin signs in once

integrations.summary: Brex card and bill spend is matched to the vendor's contract in Plinth, so unmanaged spend stands out.
integrations.syncs: Vendors and transactions, Brex to Plinth, daily; vendor records, Plinth to Brex
integrations.setup: About 10 minutes; a Brex admin signs in once

integrations.summary: A Plinth app on Zapier with triggers for new contracts, approvals and renewals, so you can wire Plinth to tools we do not connect to yet.
integrations.syncs: Events out and actions in, as they happen
integrations.setup: Minutes, by whoever owns your Zapier account

site.title: Marlow Freight Systems
site.description: Regional LTL freight across the Southeast, terminal to terminal.
site.markdown:
# Marlow Freight Systems

Regional LTL across the Southeast, with 11 terminals and next-day service between most of them.

## Our fleet

Every tractor runs Samsara telematics, so you see your freight move terminal to terminal.

## Shippers

Request a quote, track a shipment or set up a contract rate with your account manager.

careers.title: Careers at Marlow Freight
careers.description: Drivers, dock, dispatch and office roles across the Southeast.
careers.markdown:
# Careers

## Staff Accountant, Savannah

Daily work in NetSuite: vendor bills, AP runs and vendor records for about 300 suppliers.

## Sales Coordinator

Keep shipper accounts and contract rates current in Salesforce, and prepare rate confirmations for the sales team.

## Terminal Supervisor

We run the terminals on Slack and a phone. You will own one dock, one shift and the people on it.

data.headline: Plinth next to NetSuite, Salesforce and Slack at Marlow Freight
data.intro: I read your site and careers page to guess which tools Marlow already runs. The four below are guesses, so correct me where I am off. Three of them connect to Plinth today, and the fourth does not yet.

matches.change: A vendor your team approves in Plinth shows up as a NetSuite vendor record, and a signed contract raises its purchase order. The staff accountant stops retyping vendor details and sees paid status against the contract.

A shipper contract starts from the closed-won opportunity. Plinth pulls the account, the owner and the order form from Salesforce, so the sales coordinator does not email contract rates around to get them filed.
Approvals and renewal reminders land in Slack with the contract summary. A terminal supervisor or you can approve from the message, in the same channels the terminals already run on.

data.closing: If a guess is wrong, or I missed a tool, reply and I will redo this page. Twenty minutes with you and whoever owns NetSuite is enough to agree on which tool to connect first.
